ap_statistics-m01.set_intro: The relationship between the number of hours a student spent studying and the exam score, in points, is described by a least-squares regression line. Computer output for the regression is shown.

stimulus.description: Computer output for a least-squares regression

items.stem: Which of the following is the correct interpretation of the slope of the regression line?

options.text: For each additional hour of study time, the predicted exam score increases by about $5.53\%$
options.why: Treats the slope as a percent change instead of a change in the units of the response.

options.text: For each additional hour of study time, the exam score increases by exactly $5.53$ points
options.why: Claims an exact change for every individual, but the slope describes the predicted change on average.

options.text: For each additional hour of study time, the predicted exam score increases by about $5.53$ points
options.why: The slope is $5.53$, so each one-hour increase in study time goes with a predicted change of $5.53$ points in exam score.

options.text: For each additional $5.53$ points of exam score, the predicted study time increases by about $1$ hour
options.why: Reverses the roles of the explanatory and the response variables.

blueprint.subject: ap_statistics
blueprint.concept: Interpret the slope of a least-squares line in context
student_thinking: Read the slope from the Coef column next to the explanatory variable
Describe the predicted change in the response for a one-unit increase in the explanatory variable, in context and with units

key_conditions.condition: the slope is the predicted change in y for a one-unit increase in x
key_conditions.evidence: the output gives the slope in the Coef column and the stem names both variables and their units

verification.independent_path: the interpretation sentences are generated from the slope sign and units, and the slope is checked against the sign implied by the correlation

items.stem: What is the predicted exam score when study time is $6$? Round to one decimal place.

options.why: Uses the slope as the intercept and the intercept as the slope.
Leaves out the intercept and predicts with the slope times $x$ alone.
The predicted value is $\hat y = 46.4 + (5.53)(6) \approx 79.6$.
Adds the slope to the intercept instead of multiplying the slope by $x$.

blueprint.subject: ap_statistics
blueprint.concept: Predict a response value from regression output
student_thinking: Read the intercept and the slope from the Coef column
Substitute the x value into the line and round as stated

key_conditions.condition: the predicted value is intercept plus slope times x
key_conditions.evidence: the output gives both coefficients and the stem gives x

verification.independent_path: the prediction is recomputed from the printed coefficients and compared with the generating line

items.stem: What is the correlation coefficient between the two variables? Round to two decimal places.

options.why: The correlation has the same sign as the slope, so $r = \sqrt{0.49} = 0.70$.
Divides $r$ by $2$, which has no basis in the output.
Reports $r^2$ as if it were the correlation $r$.
Uses the wrong sign: the sign of $r$ must match the sign of the slope.

blueprint.subject: ap_statistics
blueprint.concept: Find the correlation coefficient from R-squared and the sign of the slope
student_thinking: Take the square root of the R-Sq value written as a proportion
Give r the same sign as the slope

key_conditions.condition: r is the square root of r squared with the sign of the slope
key_conditions.evidence: the output shows R-Sq and the slope

verification.independent_path: r is recomputed as the square root of the printed R-Sq with the slope's sign and rounded to two decimals; options are at least 0.04 apart
